rationale:
Evidence. Iteration 8 (sensors at x = ±0.030 m, 16 mm footprints, kp 6.0, kd 0.6, base_speed 1.4, ki 0.05, last_direction) is the best raced design at 123.04. Iteration 9 widened the sensors to ±0.040 m and raised kp to 8.0. It scored 75.78, so that change did not help. Its oval steering_oscillation fell to 0.203, which is the one clear gain, but oval progress dropped to 0.30 (from 0.57) and the s-bend progress to 0.17 (from 0.24). Oval max_error stayed at 0.0629, still above the 0.06 limit. So the wider reach did not give the earlier edge warning I expected, and the higher effective gain cost progress. Every trial on every track still goes off track, so score is driven mainly by progress before the first large offset. Across the series, oval max_error has stayed at 0.061 to 0.065 whatever the gain, sensor reach or kd. Iteration 0 to 1 also showed that lowering speed from 1.8 to 1.4 raised progress on all three tracks (oval 0.12 to 0.21, s-bend 0.055 to 0.098). Body width cannot relax the 0.06 m off-track limit, so the controller must hold the line at the first large offset.

Change. I return the geometry to the iteration 8 layout (±0.030 m, 16 mm, kp 6.0, kd 0.6), since that is the best-supported configuration. The one new variable is base_speed, which I lower from 1.4 to 1.2. Lower speed reduces slip and centrifugal drift in bends, and the earlier speed test showed progress rising as speed fell. ki, kd, kp, sensor weights and last_direction stay unchanged, so the result isolates speed.

Expected result. Oval max_error falls to about 0.06 or below, because less drift is needed at bend entries. Progress on the oval and s-bend rises above the iteration 8 values (0.57 and 0.24). Steering_oscillation stays near 0.27 to 0.29. Risk: 1.2 may be too slow to finish, but finishing is not reachable in this design anyway, and a full finish is far off, so progress is the target.

Hypotheses. (1) Off-track at bend entries is caused by speed-related drift, not by sensing reach or gain. (2) Line losses (1.4 oval, 1.3 s-bend) recur at the same entries and may need a search direction later.

Next steps after the race. If max_error falls below 0.06 and progress rises, keep 1.2 and consider a small kp change. If progress falls, return to base_speed 1.4 and test line_loss search_left or search_right, favouring the side the failing bends turn towards. If line losses stay at 1 or more at the same entries, that is the next lever.

Measurements wanted: steering_oscillation, max_error, line_loss_events, progress and completion_time per track, plus rms_error and control_effort.
